history.summary: A low-quantum (under $1.39M) 1,173 sqft 99LH 3BR in a quiet 288-unit Tanah Merah hilltop enclave, at $1,181 psf roughly in line with the $1,205 district median. Strong 7.1%/yr resale CAGR, but a small boutique base, an 11-min/950m MRT walk and reports of weak maintenance temper the case.
history.rating_rationale: The low $1.385M quantum is the real draw — broadest possible buyer pool and lowest absolute risk in the batch — and the 7.1%/yr resale CAGR is strong. But fundamentals are mixed: only 288 units (thinner liquidity, 68 txns), a long 11-min/950m walk to Tanah Merah MRT, and reviews flagging poor maintenance and a development that looks older than its 2004 age, plus a small pool for resident count. PSF is essentially at median ($1,181 vs $1,205), so there is no real value discount cushioning those weaknesses. Quiet hilltop exclusivity is a livability plus but not an investment catalyst. Nets to Neutral.

history.summary: Tanamera Crest (Tanah Merah, TOP 2004) 3BR 1,173 sqft at $1,385k / $1,181 psf. Web comps confirm the cheapness is real: the project's current asking-PSF range is ~$1,212-$1,425, so this unit at $1,181 sits at or below the bottom of the live range — the very_low_psf flag is a genuine discount, not a mis-scrape. Backed by 68 URA transactions and an OCR/East location near Tanah Merah MRT.
history.rating_rationale: Value leads in v3.4 and this is the strongest verified-value name in the cohort: age_adj_premium -19.4% AND independent web evidence ($1,181 psf vs project live range $1,212-$1,425, recent 6-mo avg sale ~$1.33M) both point to a true sub-market entry. psf_cohort -1.3% on 9 txns and 68 transaction base make the price discovery credible (not a 1-comp quirk). District 16 East / Tanah Merah is OCR-favoured (~+4% realized forward), with quiet, low-density family appeal and ~3.5% rental yield. The honest caveats are age (very_old_property, TOP 2004 → ~77yr lease left) and that the trailing 7.1% CAGR carries no forward weight — but the buy case rests on verified relative value plus a usable family layout in a liquid 3BR segment, not on past appreciation. That earns a Buy at medium confidence (held back from high only by lease age and the absence of a fresh, dated catalyst).

history.summary: A 1,216 sqft 3BR at Tanamera Crest (Pari Dedap Walk, D16, 99yr from 2000 so ~73yr left, TOP 2004/05, 4 blocks / 14 storeys / 288 units) asking $1,378,000 / $1,133 psf after a 5.9% cut from $1,465,000 seven weeks ago. It is the cheapest standard 3BR ask in the project and sits just below the project's own last-12-month transacted range ($1,140-$1,245 psf, avg $1,183) - a real but small ~2-4% advantage, not the -22% the algo's district channel implies. Tanamera Crest is the cheapest of 30 D16 projects on 24-month resale medians ($1,161 psf vs a $1,524 district median); that gap is a persistent location/quality level, not convergence fuel. Fairly-to-slightly-cheaply priced, verified 3.6% yield, comfortable lease - but the project's re-rating is spent (+2.7%/yr over the last two years) and 13-14 distinct 3BR units are live at once against ~6-9 sales a year. No forward edge, and a crowded exit.
history.rating_rationale:
The one backtest-validated unit-level signal - cheap-vs-peers - fires, but only faintly once the correct comp set is used, and the score's real engine does not survive scrutiny.

WHAT THE ASK IS ACTUALLY WORTH. URA gives 17 Tanamera Crest prints in 24 months, 13 of them in the tight 1,130-1,300 sqft band, median $1,161 psf (range $1,108-$1,245). The $1,133 ask is -2.4% against that - inside noise. Against the three 2026 YTD band prints (median $1,205) it is -6.0%, but all three are floor band 11 to 15 and this unit's floor is unknown, so that number is not clean. The tightest comp is the exact 1,216 sqft type: three prints ever in the cache (Oct-22 $1.250M/$1,028, Feb-23 $1.250M/$1,028, Jul-25 $1.460M/$1,200), all in floor band 01 to 05 - i.e. even the low-floor version of this exact layout last traded at $1,200 psf, so the ask is -5.6% psf / -$82,000 below its own stack's last print and there is no ask_above_own_stack_prints artifact. An independent portal read of the project's last 12 months ($1,140-$1,245 psf, average $1,183) puts the ask marginally BELOW the 12-month low. Converging all three lenses: a genuine ~2-4% discount, occasionally 5-6% depending on which floor cohort you index to. Real, verified, and too small to be an edge given the model explains <10% of forward variance.

WHY THE 792 OVERSTATES IT. The MMR's largest single component is age_value +15.6, sourced from relative_value -22.0% vs the D16 age-adjusted median. That is a project-level location discount, not a unit-level dislocation. Ranking every D16 project by 24-month resale median psf in the 1,000-1,400 sqft band (30 projects with 4+ prints), Tanamera Crest is DEAD LAST at $1,161 - below Stratford Court $1,188, The Tanamera $1,201, Casafina $1,274, East Meadows $1,292, Bayshore Park $1,297, and far below the Tanah Merah MRT-adjacent stock (Casa Merah $1,534, Optima $1,602) and the district's $1,524 all-resale median. The project has sat at the bottom of that ladder for two decades because of what it is: a 2004 build by a small developer, 770-950m uphill from Tanah Merah EW4 with no station premium (MMR itself scores mrt -2.62), 288 units, and reviews that consistently flag weak maintenance. There is no mechanism to close it. The second-largest component, appreciation +9.31 from the trailing 7.1% ura_5yr_cagr, is 2021-24 history: band median psf ran $835 (2021) -> $963 -> $1,026 -> $1,143 (2024) -> $1,178 (2025) -> $1,205 (2026 YTD), i.e. +2.7%/yr over the last two years, with momentum -0.663. Strip those two channels and the algo's own unit-level value read is psf_value +1.37 - which is exactly the ~2% the prints support.

THE EXIT IS THE REAL PROBLEM. 23 active listings in a 288-unit project, of which roughly 13-14 are distinct 3BR units, against project-wide sales of 20 (2022) -> 12 -> 10 -> 9 (2025) -> 3 YTD 2026. That is a two-to-three-year absorption overhang and it is getting worse, not better. This seller already cut 5.9% and still has not cleared. A buyer today inherits that same queue on exit in 5-7 years, when the asset is 27-29 years old with ~66-68 years of lease left. That is what caps the rating: not price, but pricing power.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD. The value case is honest and artifact-free - sqft, bedroom count and format all check out (1,216 sqft is a normal 3BR within the project's 1,163-1,647 sqft 3BR range; no PES/loft/dual-key distortion), and the very_low_psf red flag is verified benign. It is the cheapest standard 3BR ask AND the largest: $1,378k buys 1,216 sqft where $1,375k buys 1,173-1,184 sqft. Rent is confirmed by two independent sources (URA project-bed $4,150 at 0.95 confidence; live 3BR asks ~$4,300; project-wide average $3,940), so 3.61% gross / 2.16% net is real carry, not a yield artifact. Lease at 73 years leaves ~66-68 at exit, comfortably clear of the CPF pro-rating cliff - materially better than the sub-65yr OCR leaseholds in the same quantum band. The comp book is deep and transparent (113 prints in five years), so the buyer can price the entry and the exit precisely. And OCR is the favoured forward region (+3.7%/yr realized vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%) - though D16's trailing 3y (+3.9%/yr) is among the weakest in OCR, so the region credit here is thinner than the OCR label suggests.

CORRECTING THE PRIOR CALL. This project was rated Buy on 2026-06-09 at $1.39M / $1,181 psf on the reasoning that the ask sat below the live ASKING range. That method was wrong - it compared an ask to other asks, not to transacted prints. Against prints, $1,181 was ABOVE the band median. The present unit is genuinely cheaper than that one, and still only ~2-4% under market. Under current v3.5 priors the honest call for that June listing was Neutral, and it is Neutral here.

NOT AN AVOID. Nothing is overpriced, artifactual, or capital-impairing: the ask is at or slightly below its own market, the yield is verified, the lease is fine, the quantum sits in the deepest HDB-upgrader band and leaves ~$420k of the $1.8M budget unused. It is simply an ordinary asset bought at an ordinary price, into a market with more sellers than buyers and no dated catalyst. Fair entry, spent momentum, crowded exit -> Neutral.
red_flags: SUPPLY OVERHANG IS THE DOMINANT RISK: 23 active listings in a 288-unit project, ~13-14 of them distinct 3BR units, against falling project-wide volume (20 sales in 2022 -> 12 -> 10 -> 9 in 2025 -> 3 YTD 2026). That is 2-3 years of absorption standing in front of any exit. Live 3BR asks run $1,133-$1,310 psf; this seller already cut 5.9% ($1,465,000 on 07-Jun-26 -> $1,378,000 on 28-Jul-26) and has not cleared.

THE SCORE'S ENGINE IS A LOCATION LEVEL, NOT A DISCOUNT: age_value +15.6 (the largest MMR component) comes from relative_value -22.0% vs the D16 age-adjusted median. Ranked against 30 D16 projects with 4+ prints in the 1,000-1,400 sqft band over 24 months, Tanamera Crest is the CHEAPEST at $1,161 psf vs a $1,524 district median. It has been at the bottom of that ladder for 20 years. Do not credit it as convergence fuel; it is already in the price.

NOT MUCH CHEAPER THAN ITS OWN MARKET: -2.4% vs the 24-month same-size band median ($1,161 psf, 13 prints), and marginally below the independently-reported 12-month transacted range of $1,140-$1,245 psf (avg $1,183). The real discount is ~2-4%, not the -22% headline.

THE RE-RATING IS SPENT: band median psf $835 (2021) -> $963 (2022) -> $1,026 (2023) -> $1,143 (2024) -> $1,178 (2025) -> $1,205 (2026 YTD) = +2.7%/yr over the last two years, momentum -0.663. The 7.1% trailing ura_5yr_cagr the ROI table compounds is the 2021-24 OCR repricing and has ~0 forward power under v3.5 priors. See appreciation_rate_override_pct - the run's ~7.0%/yr annualized ROI is overstated by roughly half.

NO MRT PREMIUM AND NO DATED CATALYST: 770-950m (11-min walk) uphill to Tanah Merah EW4 - MMR scores mrt -2.62. The nearest future station, Bedok South TE30, is 1,715m away and is not a Tanamera Crest catalyst; the future-infrastructure channel has no measured forward power regardless. The Bayshore precinct 2-3km away is a SUPPLY event (the largest injection into D16 in decades, launching at $2,000-2,400 psf) serving a different buyer.

MAINTENANCE AND CONDITION: PropertyGuru reviews (4.1/5 across 21) repeatedly flag poor upkeep - one notes the estate 'looks like more than 10 yrs' old when it was under 7, broken BBQ charcoal trays, a pool too short to swim laps. A 22-year-old asset with a weak sinking fund is where condition decay compounds with lease decay over a 5-7yr hold.

FLOOR AND FACING UNKNOWN: both fields are 0% populated repo-wide (known broken enricher), and there is no researched stack profile for this project (stack_profile.status = not_researched). This matters because all three 2026 prints are floor band 11 to 15 and all three exact-1,216 sqft prints are floor band 01 to 05 - so which cohort is the right comp cannot be settled from the data. Mitigating: the 24-month floor gradient here is non-monotonic (01-05 median $1,198, 06-10 $1,134, 11-15 $1,178), so condition/renovation appears to swing value more than floor at this project.

NO REALSMART EVIDENCE AT ALL: the cached realsmart record for tanamera-crest (resolved 2026-07-27, ok=true) has EVERY metric null - no REALSCORE, no pct_profitable, no resale_txns, no avg_holding_yrs. Not re-fetched per instruction. So there is no downside-history evidence in either direction for this project, which is a genuine gap: the question 'has this project ever lost owners money' is unanswered here.

LEASE AND AGE: 99 years from 2000 leaves ~73 years today, not the 74 the DB record back-derives from a 2004 built year. At exit the next buyer inherits ~66-68 years - still clear of CPF pro-rating, but the asset will be 27-29 years old and competing against a D16 stock being visibly renewed at Bayshore.

MODERATE, NOT DEEP, BASE: 288 units across 4 blocks / 14 storeys, developed by TM Land Pte Ltd (a small, single-project developer with no track record to lean on). 68 URA transactions is a usable comp book but a thin annual sales rate - ~6-9 deals/yr - to absorb 13-14 competing sellers.
CARRY IS THIN AND IS NOT APPRECIATION: 3.61% gross / 2.16% net. Per v3.5 priors high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_beta -0.16); count this as income only.
catalysts: CHEAPEST STANDARD 3BR IN THE PROJECT, AND THE LARGEST: $1,133 psf vs $1,161 / $1,172 / $1,181 / $1,182 / $1,185 / $1,189 (x3) / $1,203 / $1,213 / $1,233 (x2) / $1,238 / $1,310 for the other live 3BR asks. On quantum it is the same money for more space - $1,378k buys 1,216 sqft where $1,375k buys 1,173-1,184 sqft. Entry discipline is the one genuine advantage on offer.

BELOW ITS OWN STACK'S LAST PRINT: the exact 1,216 sqft type last transacted Jul-25 at $1,460,000 / $1,200 psf on floor band 01 to 05. This ask is -5.6% psf / -$82,000 against that - i.e. cheaper than the LOW-floor version of the identical layout. No ask_above_own_stack_prints artifact, no sqft or bedroom mismatch; the very_low_psf red flag is verified benign.

VERIFIED, ARTIFACT-FREE RENTAL SUPPORT: URA project-bed rent $4,150/mo (confidence 0.95) is corroborated by live 3BR asking rents around $4,300 and a project-wide average of $3,940 across all bed types. 3.61% gross / 2.16% net is real carry, not a yield artifact - and comfortably above the sub-3% yields typical of the newer D16 stock.

DEEP, TRANSPARENT COMP BOOK: 113 URA prints in the cache since 2021, 68 in the appreciation series, 17 in 24 months, 13 in the tight size band. Entry and exit can both be priced precisely - rare at this quantum and a genuine risk reducer even though it is not a return driver.

COMFORTABLE LEASE FOR THE HOLD: 99 years from 2000 = ~73 remaining, ~66-68 at a 5-7yr exit. That stays clear of the CPF pro-rating threshold that constrains the HDB-upgrader pool - materially better than the sub-65yr OCR leaseholds competing in the same $1.3-1.5M band.

REGION AND QUANTUM: OCR is the favoured forward region under v3.5 priors (realized +3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%), buyer-pool depth reads 'deep' and is one of the few signals that survives clustering (std_beta +0.16), and $1.378M sits squarely in the deepest HDB-upgrader band while leaving ~$420k of the $1.8M budget unused. Note this is the baseline available in any OCR asset, not a Tanamera Crest edge - and D16's trailing 3y (+3.9%/yr) is among the weakest in OCR.

QUIET, LOW-DENSITY SETTING WITH DUAL-LINE ACCESS: 4 blocks on a hillside next to a landed estate (a live rental listing for this exact 1,216 sqft type advertises a landed-estate view), consistently praised in reviews as 'peaceful and quiet'; Tanah Merah EW4 (EWL + Changi branch) and Bedok Reservoir DT30 both reachable. Supports the owner-occupier family bid that a 1,216 sqft 3BR depends on for exit.

Forward positives are region (OCR +3.7%/yr realized) and buyer-pool depth; forward drags are D16's weak trailing 3y (+3.9%/yr, among the softest in OCR), leasehold decay from 73 to ~66-68 years across the hold, ageing from 22 to 27-29 years against a district being renewed at Bayshore, and - most concretely - a standing queue of 13-14 competing 3BR sellers that will still be there on exit.
